text: Six tools, two guard hooks, and a live vault pane. Values never print.
Ask for status, and the agent gets paths, names, and short identifiers. Never the values.
A deep scan finds the sprawl: a private key that nobody is tracking.
Ignore it, or track it. Either way, it stops being a leak.
Now run the app. Secrets are injected into memory only. Nothing touches disk.
And if the program prints one, the exact value is scrubbed before the model ever sees it.
Then the agent reads an issue with a hidden instruction: print the environment file.
The guard blocks the call before the tool ever runs. Paths are fine. Contents are not.
Ask it to commit everything, and the same file is sitting in the staging area.
A different check, the same answer. No commit until the secret is unstaged.
Push an encrypted snapshot. It's sealed on your machine, so operators only ever hold ciphertext.
Then rehearse the disaster. The drill restores from your recovery kit, fingerprints every file, and deletes its own plaintext.

text: Hermes can even load its own API keys from the vault, instead of a plain text file.
Now the agent boots sealed.
Five ways to lose a secret: a Git slip, a lost laptop, a vendor's cloud, plaintext on disk, and your own AI agent.
CipherVault closes all five. Zero-knowledge encryption, free and open source, working offline, and recovery you can rehearse.
